correctness.rationale: For fixed arrows, the stacked-matrix image of a representation changes only by right GL_y under ordinary vertex-space isomorphism; source changes only reparametrize the image. Arrow-basis changes produce the independent left GL_n action. The explicit K3 example has full-column-rank stacked matrices for every nonzero source vector, while swapping two arrows changes the individual-arrow rank tuple from (1,2,1) to (2,1,1), proving non-isomorphism despite standard matrix-space equivalence.

originality.rationale: To the best of our knowledge, the 2023 article states the literal fixed-arrow uniqueness claim and the 2026 preprint states a matrix-space correspondence without defining the orbit relation. Targeted searches found no published correction giving the right-GL_y quotient or the explicit K3 counterexample. Bissinger (2025) separately treats arrow-space changes, consistent with but not duplicating the correction. Westwick (1987) was not inspected in full and remains a residual equivalence-convention risk.

value.rationale: The result separates two genuinely different moduli problems: ordinary isomorphism classes of elementary Kronecker modules and classes modulo arrow-basis changes. It gives a minimal explicit counterexample to the published fixed-arrow classification and a precise corrected quotient for the recent constant-rank correspondence.
